# Sirach Chapter 8 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 8 (19 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.1: "contend" vs. "quarrel" vs. "pick a fight"

**EMET:** "Do not contend with a powerful man"
**LOGOS:** "Do not quarrel with someone powerful"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't pick a fight with someone powerful"
**Issue:** Greek mē machesai = "do not fight." EMET "contend" is slightly elevated; LOGOS "quarrel" more common; PNEUMA "pick a fight" is colloquial. Consensus: "Do not contend with a powerful person."

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.2: "perverted the minds" vs. "corrupted the minds"

**EMET:** "has perverted the minds of kings"
**LOGOS:** "has corrupted the minds of kings"
**PNEUMA:** "led kings astray"
**Issue:** Greek metetrepsato kardias basileōn = "turned aside the hearts of kings." "Perverted" (EMET) and "corrupted" (LOGOS) are both accurate; PNEUMA "led astray" is weaker. Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.3: "full of words" vs. "loudmouth"

**EMET:** "a man who is full of words"
**LOGOS:** "a loudmouth"
**PNEUMA:** "someone who never shuts up"
**Issue:** Greek lalon = "one who speaks much/babbles." EMET is literal; LOGOS is more idiomatic; PNEUMA is very colloquial. Consensus: "someone full of words."

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.4: "jest" vs. "make jokes"

**EMET:** "Do not jest with an uneducated person"
**LOGOS:** "Do not make jokes with an uneducated person"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't mock or joke with uneducated people"
**Issue:** Greek mē paizē = "do not play/jest." LOGOS/EMET are close. PNEUMA adds "mock." Consensus: "Do not jest with an uneducated person."

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.5: "reproach" vs. "rub it in"

**EMET:** "Do not reproach a man who is turning away from sin"
**LOGOS:** "Do not reproach someone who is turning back from sin"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't rub it in when someone is turning away from sin"
**Issue:** Minor. PNEUMA's colloquialism is too casual for a formal wisdom saying. Consensus: EMET/LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.6: "dishonor a man in his old age" vs. "scorn an old person"

**EMET:** "Do not dishonor a man in his old age"
**LOGOS:** "Do not scorn an old person"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't despise an old person"
**Issue:** Greek mē atimasēs = "do not dishonor/disrespect." "Scorn" and "despise" are more specific. "Dishonor" (EMET) is more literal. Consensus: "Do not dishonor an old person."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.8: "discourse of the wise" vs. "what wise people have to say"

**EMET:** "discourse of the wise"
**LOGOS:** "discourse of the wise"
**PNEUMA:** "what wise people have to say"
**Issue:** Greek diegēma sophōn = "discourse/narration of the wise." EMET/LOGOS agree. Consensus: "Do not overlook the discourse of the wise."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.9: "their fathers" vs. "their parents"

**EMET:** "they themselves have learned from their fathers"
**LOGOS:** "they themselves learned from their parents"
**PNEUMA:** "They learned from their own parents"
**Issue:** Greek para patros autōn = "from their fathers." EMET is literal. LOGOS/PNEUMA gender-neutralize. Consensus: "they themselves learned from their fathers" — the patrilineal tradition is intended.

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.10: "kindle the coals" vs. "stoke the fire"

**EMET:** "Do not kindle the coals of a sinner"
**LOGOS:** "Do not stoke the fire of a sinner"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't fan the flames around a sinner"
**Issue:** Greek mē ekkaē anthraka hamartōlou = "do not kindle the coals of a sinner." EMET is most literal. "Coals" (Greek anthrax) is the specific image — live coals that can reignite. Consensus: EMET.

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.11: "get up against" vs. "rise up against"

**EMET:** "Do not get up against a shameless person"
**LOGOS:** "Do not rise up against the shameless"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't rise to confront someone who is shameless"
**Issue:** Greek mē anastēs katananti anapaideutou = "do not stand up before the shameless." LOGOS is more elegant. Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.12: "stronger than you" vs. "more powerful than you"

**EMET:** "Do not lend to someone who is stronger than you"
**LOGOS:** "Do not lend to someone more powerful than you"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't lend to someone more powerful than you"
**Issue:** Greek kreissoni sou = "stronger/mightier than you." "More powerful" (LOGOS) is better for social context. Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.15: "reckless fellow" vs. "reckless person"

**EMET:** "Do not travel with a reckless fellow"
**LOGOS:** "Do not travel alongside a reckless person"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't travel with a reckless person"
**Issue:** Minor. Greek akriton = "undiscerning/reckless." Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.16: "no help" vs. "deserted place" vs. "uninhabited country"

**EMET:** "where there is no help, he will strike you down"
**LOGOS:** "in a deserted place they may cut you down"
**PNEUMA:** "in a place with no witnesses, you could be the victim"
**Issue:** Greek eis erēmian = "into the wilderness/desert." The point is both geographic isolation and lack of witnesses. LOGOS "deserted place" is closest. Consensus: "in an uninhabited place they may cut you down."

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.19: "open your heart" vs. "pour out your heart"

**EMET:** "Do not open your heart to every person"
**LOGOS:** "Do not pour out your heart to everyone"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't open yourself up completely to just anyone"
**Issue:** Greek mē ekteinēs = "do not extend/open." EMET's "open your heart" is the common idiom and is literal enough. Consensus: EMET.

---
